description: We operate as a collaborative lab where clear documentation, smart design, and hardware-software integration come together. To complement our technical foundation, we are looking for teammates who bring strengths in CAD modeling, 3D prototyping, UI/UX design, or project research. If you enjoy building real-world solutions and bringing ideas to life, you'll fit right in!
summary:
We developed Outpost Cadet, an immersive, browser-based 3D simulation that transforms users into astronauts managing a deep-space outpost. Addressing the challenge of making space science deeply interactive, this prototype moves beyond simple quizzes by forcing players to make authentic engineering trade-offs. Using simulated NASA data and real-world physics, players must meticulously balance life support, radiation shielding, and power grid efficiency to survive dynamic space weather hazards like coronal mass ejections and oxygen leaks.

This project is crucial because it bridges the gap between entertainment and STEM education. By experiencing the harsh realities of space—where there are no perfect choices, only calculated compromises—young learners organically grasp complex concepts like resource management, thermodynamic limits, and aerospace engineering. Outpost Cadet inspires the Artemis generation by proving that space exploration relies just as much on critical thinking and problem-solving as it does on rocket launches, all delivered in a highly accessible, zero-installation web environment.
details:
• Core Functionality: Operates as a browser-based 3D simulator where users act as a base commander on a planetary outpost, bypassing simple point-and-click mechanics in favor of complex UI consoles
  • Dynamic Response: Forces players to react in real-time to simulated space weather emergencies, demonstrating that every action has an engineering consequence.
  • Educational Benefits: Transforms abstract mathematical and physics concepts into active survival mechanics, proving that routing emergency power to radiation shields requires sacrificing resources elsewhere, like hydroponic crop yields.
  • Target Impact: Aims to cultivate STEM interest among the Artemis generation by reframing space exploration as a test of meticulous engineering, critical thinking, and closed-loop systems management rather than just rocket launches.
  • Tech Stack: Developed using JavaScript, React.js for UI state management, and Tailwind CSS for HUD styling. The 3D environment is powered by WebGL via Three.js, with procedural sound via the Web Audio API, state management by Zustand, and hosted globally via Vercel.
  • Creative Design: Features "diegetic" interfaces—meaning engineering panels, sliders, and telemetry screens exist seamlessly within the 3D world rather than as generic 2D pop-up menus.
  • Scientific Integration: Incorporates research from NASA's DONKI (Space Weather Database) to ensure in-game hazards mirror real-world physics, replacing generic "Game Over" screens with scientifically accurate evaluation screens that explain the physics of the player's failure.
  • Design Considerations: The team carefully balanced the need for AAA-quality 3D visuals against the necessity of high accessibility, heavily optimizing the application to ensure it runs smoothly at 60 FPS on standard school Chromebooks without requiring any software installation.
